test_cases.objective: To verify that the system accurately tracks inventory quantities in real-time through standard database updates.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has appropriate access to the inventory management module.
At least one item is set up in the item master.

test_steps.action: Perform a manual inventory adjustment (e.g., add 10 units of a specific item).
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the updated inventory quantity for the item within 30 seconds.

test_steps.action: Perform a picking transaction to remove 5 units of the same item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the reduced inventory quantity for the item within 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory quantities are updated and displayed accurately in real-time after each transaction.
All inventory updates are reflected within the specified 30-second timeframe.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-006: Track inventory quantities in real-time using standard database updates.
URS-INV-016: Maintain inventory audit trail using vendor's standard logging functionality.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure no data loss or corruption during inventory updates.
Verify that the audit trail accurately records all inventory adjustments.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Generation for Inventory Movements
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can generate standard inventory movement reports using pre-built templates within the specified time.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has appropriate access to reporting functions.
Sufficient inventory movement transactions have occurred to populate a report (e.g., receipts, picks, adjustments).

test_steps.action: Navigate to the reporting module and select the 'Inventory Movement Report' using a pre-built template.
test_steps.expected_result: The system initiates the generation of the inventory movement report.

test_steps.action: Execute the report generation process.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory movement report is generated successfully within 5 minutes.

test_steps.action: Review the generated report for accuracy and completeness of inventory movement data.
test_steps.expected_result: The report accurately reflects all recorded inventory movements within the specified date range and includes all relevant details (e.g., item, quantity, transaction type, date).
data_to_capture: Sample of data entries from the report
Comparison of report data with transaction logs

acceptance_criteria: The inventory movement report is generated within the 5-minute timeframe.
The generated report accurately and completely displays all inventory movement transactions.
The report uses a standard pre-built template as defined by the vendor.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-009: Create inventory movement reports using pre-built templates.
URS-INV-016: Maintain inventory audit trail using vendor's standard logging functionality.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the report data is consistent with the underlying transaction data.
Verify that the report does not omit any critical movement details.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly implements First-In-First-Out (FIFO) inventory rotation for stock management.
prerequisites: System is configured with at least two batches of the same item with different received dates.
User has appropriate permissions to manage inventory.

test_steps.action: Add a new batch of a specific item to the inventory, ensuring it is the most recently received.
test_steps.expected_result: The new batch is successfully added to the inventory with its correct received date.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock deduction or picking process for a quantity of the item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system deducts inventory from the oldest available batch first, adhering to FIFO principles.
data_to_capture: Batch Number(s) from which inventory was deducted

test_steps.action: Review the inventory levels and batch status after the deduction.
test_steps.expected_result: The oldest batch is depleted before the newer batches, and the total inventory quantity is reduced accordingly.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully deducts inventory from the oldest batch first.
Inventory quantities are accurately updated after the deduction.
The FIFO rotation logic is demonstrably applied.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-003: Implement First-In-First-Out (FIFO) inventory rotation using vendor default algorithms.
data_integrity_requirements: Batch dates must be correctly recorded and utilized.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly implements First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) inventory rotation for expiry date management.
prerequisites: System is configured with at least two batches of the same item with different expiry dates.
User has appropriate permissions to manage inventory.

test_steps.action: Add a new batch of a specific item to the inventory, ensuring it has the earliest expiry date among available batches.
test_steps.expected_result: The new batch is successfully added to the inventory with its correct expiry date.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock deduction or picking process for a quantity of the item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system deducts inventory from the batch with the earliest expiry date first, adhering to FEFO principles.
data_to_capture: Batch Number(s) from which inventory was deducted

test_steps.action: Review the inventory levels and batch status after the deduction.
test_steps.expected_result: The batch with the earliest expiry date is depleted before batches with later expiry dates, and the total inventory quantity is reduced accordingly.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully deducts inventory from the batch with the earliest expiry date first.
Inventory quantities are accurately updated after the deduction.
The FEFO rotation logic is demonstrably applied.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-004: Support First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) rotation for expiry date management.
data_integrity_requirements: Expiry dates must be correctly recorded and utilized.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Barcode Scanning Integration for Inventory Updates
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly updates inventory quantities when using barcode scanning functionality.
prerequisites: Barcode scanner is connected and configured.
Inventory items have valid barcodes assigned.
System is operational and accessible.

test_steps.action: Scan the barcode of a specific inventory item.
test_steps.expected_result: The system recognizes the scanned barcode and displays the corresponding item details.
data_to_capture: Item details displayed by the system

test_steps.action: Perform an inventory transaction (e.g., receiving or issuing) using the scanned barcode.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory quantity for the scanned item is updated accurately in the system reflecting the transaction.

test_steps.action: Verify the inventory quantity update in the system's inventory records.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory quantity displayed in the system matches the expected quantity after the transaction.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully recognizes and processes scanned barcodes.
Inventory quantities are updated accurately in real-time after barcode-driven transactions.
No errors or discrepancies are observed during the barcode scanning and inventory update process.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-007: Support barcode scanning using vendor's barcode integration module.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurate after barcode scanning operations.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Cycle Count Schedule Generation and Execution
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can generate cycle count schedules based on predefined criteria and that these schedules can be executed.
prerequisites: Sufficient inventory data exists in the system.
Cycle count parameters (e.g., frequency, item selection criteria) are configured.
System is operational and accessible.

test_steps.action: Configure the system to generate a cycle count schedule for a specific date range or criteria.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a cycle count schedule listing items to be counted.
data_to_capture: Generated cycle count schedule (list of items, locations)

test_steps.action: Review the generated cycle count schedule for accuracy and completeness.
test_steps.expected_result: The schedule includes the expected items and locations based on the configured criteria.

test_steps.action: Initiate the cycle count process for a selected item or location from the schedule.
test_steps.expected_result: The system allows for the initiation of a cycle count for the selected item/location.

test_steps.action: Perform a physical count of the selected item/location and enter the count into the system.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the entered physical count.

test_steps.action: Verify the system's reconciliation of the physical count against the system's recorded quantity.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accurately identifies any discrepancies between the physical count and the system's recorded quantity.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully generates cycle count schedules based on configured parameters.
The generated schedules are accurate and comprehensive.
The system allows for the initiation and execution of cycle counts.
Discrepancies between physical counts and system records are correctly identified.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-008: Create inventory movement reports using pre-built templates.
data_integrity_requirements: Cycle count schedules must accurately reflect items and locations for counting.
Discrepancies identified during cycle counts must be accurately reported.

test_cases.test_name: Verify User Access Controls and Role-Based Security
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system enforces user access controls and role-based security as defined by vendor specifications.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User accounts with different roles (e.g., Administrator, Warehouse Operator, Viewer) are created.
Documentation for vendor's role-based security is available.

test_steps.action: Log in to the system using an Administrator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator can access all system functionalities and settings.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Warehouse Operator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Warehouse Operator can perform inventory management tasks (e.g., receiving, picking, adjustments) but cannot access administrative settings or user management.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Viewer account.
test_steps.expected_result: Viewer can only view inventory data and reports, with no ability to modify any data or access system settings.

test_steps.action: Attempt to perform an action outside the assigned role's permissions for each user type.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents the action and displays an appropriate error message indicating insufficient permissions.

acceptance_criteria: Users can only access functionalities permitted by their assigned roles.
Unauthorized access attempts are blocked with clear error messages.
System maintains segregation of duties based on user roles.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-017: Support user access controls through vendor's role-based security.
data_integrity_requirements: User access controls prevent unauthorized data modifications.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Inventory Audit Trail and Transaction History Archiving
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains a comprehensive audit trail of all inventory transactions and supports the archiving of transaction history.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient inventory transactions have been performed to test archiving.
Documentation for vendor's logging and data retention policies is available.

test_steps.action: Perform a series of inventory transactions (e.g., receiving, issuing, adjustments, transfers) using different user accounts.
test_steps.expected_result: Each transaction is recorded in the system's audit trail, including user, timestamp, transaction type, and affected items/quantities.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for each transaction

test_steps.action: Access and review the audit trail for a specific transaction.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail accurately reflects all details of the performed transaction.
data_to_capture: Audit trail details for reviewed transaction

test_steps.action: Generate an inventory movement report for a defined period that includes archived transactions.
test_steps.expected_result: The report includes all relevant transactions, demonstrating that archived data is accessible for reporting purposes.

test_steps.action: Verify the system's data retention policy is applied, and older transactions are archived according to the defined policy.
test_steps.expected_result: Transactions older than the defined retention period are moved to an archive, and the system's active transaction log reflects this.

acceptance_criteria: All inventory transactions are logged in the audit trail with complete details.
The audit trail is accurate and tamper-evident.
Archived transaction history is accessible for reporting and auditing.
The system adheres to the defined data retention policies.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-016: Maintain inventory audit trail using vendor's standard logging functionality.
URS-INV-019: Archive transaction history using vendor's data retention policies.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail ensures traceability of all inventory changes.
Archiving ensures historical data is preserved according to policy.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Support for Multiple Storage Locations and Location Master Setup
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly supports the setup and management of multiple storage locations and their associated master data.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has administrative privileges to configure locations.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the location master setup section of the inventory management system.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the interface for creating, editing, and viewing storage locations.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the location master setup interface.

test_steps.action: Create a new storage location with a unique identifier, description, and type (e.g., 'Warehouse A - Zone 1', 'Cold Storage - Rack 3').
test_steps.expected_result: The new storage location is successfully created and listed in the system.
data_to_capture: Details of the created location (ID, description, type).

test_steps.action: Assign an existing item to the newly created storage location.
test_steps.expected_result: The item is successfully associated with the new storage location, and its inventory can be tracked within that location.
data_to_capture: Item ID and the assigned storage location.

test_steps.action: Attempt to create a duplicate storage location identifier.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents the creation of a duplicate location identifier and displays an appropriate error message.
data_to_capture: Error message displayed by the system.

acceptance_criteria: The system allows for the creation and management of multiple distinct storage locations.
Each storage location can be uniquely identified and described.
Items can be successfully assigned to specific storage locations.
The system prevents the creation of duplicate storage location identifiers.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-010: Support multiple storage locations with standard location master setup.
data_integrity_requirements: Location master data must be accurate and unique.
Item-to-location assignments must be correctly recorded.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Reorder Alerts Based on Minimum Stock Levels
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates timely and accurate reorder alerts when inventory quantities fall below predefined minimum stock levels.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
At least one item is configured with a minimum stock level.
User has access to view inventory levels and alerts.

test_steps.action: Identify an item in the system that has a minimum stock level configured (e.g., 50 units).
test_steps.expected_result: The item's current inventory quantity and its configured minimum stock level are visible.
data_to_capture: Item ID, current quantity, and minimum stock level.

test_steps.action: Manually reduce the inventory quantity of the identified item to a level below its minimum stock level (e.g., 49 units).
test_steps.expected_result: The system updates the item's inventory quantity to the new value.

test_steps.action: Access the system's alerting or notification area, or check for any visual indicators of alerts.
test_steps.expected_result: A reorder alert is generated for the item whose stock level has fallen below the minimum threshold.
data_to_capture: Details of the generated alert (item ID, alert type, timestamp).

test_steps.action: Verify that the alert accurately reflects the item and the condition (below minimum stock).
test_steps.expected_result: The alert correctly identifies the item and indicates that its stock is below the minimum level.

test_steps.action: Increase the inventory quantity of the item back above the minimum stock level.
test_steps.expected_result: The system updates the inventory quantity, and the reorder alert is cleared or updated accordingly (depending on system configuration).
data_to_capture: Status of the alert after quantity increase.

acceptance_criteria: The system generates a reorder alert when an item's inventory quantity drops below its configured minimum stock level.
The generated alert accurately identifies the item and the reason for the alert.
The alert is visible to authorized users.
Alerts are cleared or updated appropriately when stock levels are replenished.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-011: Generate reorder alerts based on minimum stock levels using standard alerting.
data_integrity_requirements: Minimum stock levels must be accurately configured and maintained.
Alerts must be generated based on real-time inventory data.
